local_facts.claim: The USGS description of the Austin quadrangle divides the area into a higher western district of the Edwards Plateau and a lower eastern district at the Coastal Plain margin. The Balcones escarpment runs through the Austin area as a major topographic and structural boundary.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A house west of the divide can encounter shallow limestone while an east-side lot may have a very different soil profile. An Austin foundation assessment has to follow the actual lot and structure rather than applying one repair method across the city.
local_facts.title: The Balcones boundary makes Austin ground change fast

local_facts.claim: A City of Austin geologic appendix says the Taylor Group in the Austin area weathers to calcareous, montmorillonitic clay and marly clay generally referred to as Taylor Clay. The USDA's Houston Black series description identifies a Travis County type location and classifies the soil as smectitic clay.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Taylor Clay and Houston Black soil are not generic dirt conditions. Their clay mineralogy and moisture response make it important to measure the structure and understand the site before selecting stabilization work.
local_facts.title: East Austin-area clay has a named geologic story

local_facts.claim: A City of Austin rainfall study records 19.68 inches at Camp Mabry in 2011. The city's 2022 Watershed Protection annual report also records 2.96 inches of rain in one hour at Camp Mabry after 51 days with no measurable rainfall.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Long dry periods followed by abrupt rainfall can change moisture conditions around a clay-supported foundation. The useful response is to document structural changes over time and diagnose the house itself, not to assume every symptom has the same cause.
local_facts.title: Austin records sharp dry-to-wet moisture swings

anchors.label: Who is supposed to design the repair
anchors.detail: The Texas Section ASCE guidelines, Version 2 adopted May 1, 2009, state that the evaluation and repair design shall be performed by a professional engineer licensed in the State of Texas, and that the sealing engineer is the engineer of record with approval authority over changes.
anchors.source_name: Texas Section ASCE guidelines for the evaluation and repair of residential foundations

anchors.label: The number an engineer measures against
anchors.detail: Those same guidelines borrow the residential code deflection limit of L over 360 as the analogous limit for a foundation profile, and note that a floor slope greater than 1 percent is usually noticeable. Cracks alone are not the test.

anchors.label: Clay content in the Austin soil series
anchors.detail: The USDA official series description puts clay at 35 to 55 percent in the particle-size control section of the Austin series, mapped in the Blackland Prairies of Texas. That fraction is the mechanism behind seasonal slab movement here.
anchors.source_name: USDA official soil series description, Austin series

anchors.label: How the city classifies the work
anchors.detail: Austin lists foundation repair among the residential minor repairs handled through a Residential Express Building Permit, so the paperwork is quick but it is still a permitted trade with an inspection attached.
anchors.source_name: City of Austin types of permits
